questions.q: List three examples of infrastructure from your daily life.
questions.a: Roads, schools, and electricity supply. A wrong answer (like "a tractor" or "a book") reveals the student confuses "tools used for production" with "infrastructure that serves the entire society."

questions.q: Why is infrastructure called the "backbone" of an economy?
questions.a: It is called the backbone because it provides the necessary support for all other economic activities to function, just as a spine supports a body. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks infrastructure is just a luxury rather than a fundamental requirement for trade and production.

questions.q: If a city had no communication networks (like internet or phones), how would a local shopkeeper be affected?
questions.a: The shopkeeper could not order new stock from wholesalers, inform customers about sales, or use digital payments. A wrong answer indicates the student fails to connect infrastructure to the efficiency of business operations.

questions.q: Compare the impact of a road network on a farmer versus a factory worker.
questions.a: The farmer needs roads to transport perishable crops to the market; the factory worker needs roads to transport finished goods and reach the factory safely. A wrong answer suggests the student views infrastructure as isolated pieces rather than a connected system.

questions.q: Is a private bicycle "infrastructure"? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, it is not infrastructure because it is a private asset that benefits one person, whereas infrastructure refers to public systems (like bridges or power grids) that benefit the entire society. A wrong answer suggests confusion between personal property and public utility.

questions.q: Create a plan for a new village: which two pieces of infrastructure would you prioritize to help local farmers grow their income, and why?
questions.a: The student should select infrastructure like "cold storage" (to prevent spoilage) and "paved roads" (to reach markets). Poor answers will name things that are not infrastructure or fail to explain the economic benefit to the farmer.
